title: Machine-learning models estimate one-year target-lesion failure risk after coronary intervention
summary: Five models were trained on 35,389 patients in the global e-ULTIMASTER percutaneous coronary intervention registry. On a random 20% test split, gradient boosting had an AUC of 0.72 (95% CI 0.69–0.75) for one-year target-lesion failure; component AUCs were 0.82 for cardiac death, 0.75 for target-vessel myocardial infarction, and 0.68 for clinically driven revascularization. The study lacks external validation outside this registry and calls for prospective evaluation; it does not establish clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Gradient boosting, linear discriminant analysis, naive Bayes, logistic regression, and k-nearest neighbors

evidence.tested: Five risk models were evaluated on a held-out random test subset of the e-ULTIMASTER registry, with discrimination and calibration assessed.
evidence.unknown: The authors report no external validation outside the registry and state that prospective evaluation is warranted; clinical utility is unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Learned risk models estimate one-year target-lesion failure and its component outcomes from patient and procedural characteristics.

source_review.scope: Full primary publisher article, including Methods, Results, author affiliations and publication history
